newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wallis backs single regulator for some operations.
newsitem.headline: Wallis backs single regulator for some operations.

text.p: Australia's Wallis inquiry into the financial system on Wednesday recommended a single agency should oversee some financial regulatory operations.

The report also said the Reserve Bank of Australia should remain responsible for the stability of the financial system, and recommended that the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) should administer competition laws.

The inquiry also recommended institutions should be free to set fees without government intervention; that super funds should not be required to invest in small to medium enterprises; and urged prudential regulation on deposit taking, insurance and super funds.

The report said a new prudential agency, the Corporations and Financial Services Commission (CSFC), should be established to provide Commonwealth regulation of corporations, financial market integrity and consumer protection.

"It should combine the existing market integrity, corporations and consumer protection roles of the Australian Securities Commission (ASC), the Insurance Superannuation Commission (ISC) and the Australian Payments System Council," the report said.
The report said the Reserve Bank should retain overall responsibility for the stability of the financial system, in consultation as necessary with the Treasurer and other financial authorities.
"The central bank is best placed to ensure the stability of the financial system and manage systemic risks," it said.
The report also recommended the ACCC should continue to administer the competition laws for the financial system, as for other sectors.

It said institutions should have the freedom to set fees and charges for retail financial and transaction services based generally on the cost of the provision of those services without government intervention or suasion.
The report said superannuation funds should not be required to invest in small and medium sized enterprises (SMEs).

"Superannuation investment decisions should continue to be a matter for the trustees of the fund concerned, subject to the requirement of the Superannuation Industry (Supervision) Act 1993 that they invest prudently in a properly diversified portfolio," it said.
The report said prudential regulation should be imposed on deposit taking, insurance and superannuation.

Led by businessman Stan Wallis, the inquiry into Australia's financial system finished its report last month. The report was considered by the Howard government earlier this week and released by Treasurer Peter Costello in Canberra on Wednesday.

"Prudential regulation should be imposed on institutions licensed to conduct the general business of deposit-taking from the public, or offering capital-backed life products, general insurance products or superannuation investments," the report said.
